Bombardier — Repeated Bailouts. Billions in Public Support, Executive Bonuses, Job Cuts. Bombardier has received multiple rounds of government financial support — including federal and Quebec government loans, equity investments, and contracts. During periods of government support, Bombardier paid executive bonuses that drew public criticism. The company also cut thousands of jobs while receiving public money. Bombardier eventually sold its commercial aviation business (C Series, now Airbus A220) and its rail transportation division — raising questions about the return on public investment. The pattern: public money flows in, executive compensation continues, jobs are cut, and the business units are eventually sold to foreign corporations. Primary sources: federal and Quebec public accounts, parliamentary committee transcripts, Bombardier annual reports and press releases on the C Series transaction.

EV Battery Plants — $15B+ in Subsidies. Volkswagen, Stellantis, Honda — Matched or Exceeded US IRA. The federal government committed over $15 billion in production subsidies for electric vehicle battery manufacturing plants — Volkswagen PowerCo in St. Thomas, Stellantis-LG in Windsor, and Honda in Alliston. These subsidies were justified as necessary to match US Inflation Reduction Act incentives. The per-job cost of these subsidies has been calculated in the hundreds of thousands of dollars. The PBO has examined the fiscal impact. The subsidies flow to multinational corporations whose global operations generate billions in annual revenue.
